transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because... things have just gone very quiet for me lately. 

The part of me that used to reach out to people, or... take pleasure in things... it just feels like it's faded. My work, yoga, going to galleries... even just journaling. I don't really care about them right now. I'm mostly just... moving through my obligations. That's really it.
How long have you been feeling this way — this loss of interest and pleasure in things?

I suppose it's been... about eight months. That's when we took my older relative into our apartment. Since then, just... this whole change in how I'm thinking, and working... connecting with people. It's been going on since then.
During these past eight months, have you been feeling persistently sad or down in your mood, or is it mainly that you've lost interest in things without necessarily feeling depressed?

I don't think I've been sad. Just... flat, I suppose. 

I wouldn't really call it being depressed. It's mostly just... not having the interest to do much anymore. That's all.
Even though you say you haven't felt sad, have there been any times during these eight months when your mood has been noticeably low or down — even if it wasn't the main thing you were experiencing?
No, not really. I just... I don't feel much of anything. It's not sadness, it's just... empty.
Before these past eight months, have you ever had a period lasting weeks or months where you felt this same kind of emptiness, flatness, or loss of interest in things?
No... I don't think so. Just... just these last eight months, really.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep — like sleeping more or less than usual, or trouble falling asleep?
No... I don't think so. My sleep is mostly just... the same as always, I guess. I haven't really noticed anything different.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?
No, not really. I... I eat about the same, I guess. My weight hasn't changed.
Since your older relative moved in, have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself about anything — either about the situation with them, or about other things in general?
No, not really. I don't... I haven't been feeling guilty or anything like that. It's just... the way things are right now.

Over these past eight months, have you noticed changes in your energy level or how you move and think — like feeling more tired or sluggish, or perhaps the opposite, feeling more restless or agitated?
I haven't noticed anything like that. My energy is... it's about the same, I suppose. I don't feel unusually tired or agitated... just getting through the day.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, making decisions, or remembering things over these past eight months?
No, I don't think so. I can still focus on... whatever I need to do. It's not really a problem.

Besides the loss of interest in activities, have you been experiencing any physical symptoms or bodily complaints — like pain, fatigue, dizziness, or other physical sensations — over these past eight months?
Not really. Physically, I'm... fine. I haven't noticed any pain or dizziness or anything like that.
How much distress or upset has this flatness and loss of interest been causing you? Has it been significantly interfering with your ability to do your work or manage your daily responsibilities?

I suppose it's... noticeable. I'm still showing up to work, but... I missed a few grant deadlines recently. And my supervisor... she moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. So... I guess I'm not functioning at my usual level. It's... frustrating, but I just don't have it in me right now.
When your older relative first moved in eight months ago, did you notice the flatness and loss of interest start right around that time, or did it develop gradually over weeks after they arrived?
I'm... not really sure. I didn't exactly keep track of it. It's hard to say if it was right away or... later. I just know it's been a while.
Since your older relative moved in, how would you describe the level of stress or burden you've been experiencing with that situation? Do you feel overwhelmed by having them in your apartment?
I don't know... it's just a situation. I wouldn't say I'm overwhelmed. It's just... someone living there. I deal with it.
Have you been experiencing any worry, anxiety, or nervous tension over these past eight months — even if it's not the main thing you're noticing?
No... not really. I mean, I guess I have normal worries, but... nothing major. I haven't been particularly anxious or nervous. Just... dealing with things as they come.

When you say you feel 'empty' and 'flat,' is there any sense that your mood itself has shifted — like a heaviness or darkness to how you feel — or is it purely just an absence of interest without any change in your mood tone?
I wouldn't really call it heavy, or... dark. It's just... empty. I don't really notice a mood at all, to be honest. Just kind of... nothing.

When you describe feeling 'empty,' do you experience that emptiness as something painful or distressing in itself — like an ache or void that bothers you — or is it more like you simply don't feel much of anything, without the emptiness itself causing you distress?
No... it doesn't hurt. It's not distressing, really. I just... I don't feel much of anything. It doesn't really bother me. It's just how it is.

When you think back over these eight months, has there been any time when you felt down, sad, or low — even briefly or mildly — or has it truly been only the flatness and lack of interest without any sadness at all?
No, I haven't really felt sad. Or down. It's... just the flatness. I haven't noticed any sadness at all.

When you say you don't feel much of anything, does that include not feeling sad, but also not feeling happy or content either — or is there a difference in how you experience those different emotions?

I suppose... yeah, it includes that. I don't really feel happy, either. 

I guess that's what finally brought me in. It's just... the part of me that used to reach out for people, or take pleasure in things... my work, yoga, going to galleries, even just journaling... it's all gone very quiet. I don't really feel a difference between emotions anymore. I'm mostly just... moving through obligations.
